scenarios.title: Identify and mount the assigned volume
scenarios.summary: Repair a saved volume identity and make the intended filesystem available without disturbing a healthy peer.
scenarios.objective: Work is UUID 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111: writable at /work, automatic, mounted when finished. Reports is UUID 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222: read-only at /reports, automatic and still mounted when finished. Repair the saved work source and make every saved entry select its intended volume after device names change. Keep filesystem types, identities and the supplied last two numbers unchanged. Save edits, inspect the live mounts and check the complete configuration.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the first reported mismatch, then compare the ticket, saved file and live table. Saving, mounting and testing a fresh copy are different actions; retry after repairing the relevant state.
steps: Inspect and repair the saved configuration
Make the live mounts match and verify
scenarios.explanation: The UUID identifies the work volume independently of its current connection name. Saving repairs the persistent instruction; mounting makes it live. Reports keeps its intended identity and read-only policy. The independent test copies verify the saved choices after device-name changes without replacing the current session.
hints: Compare the ticket UUIDs with blkid and read the saved file before changing a source.
Saving a correct entry does not create its live mount. Inspect mount output to see which target is missing.
A current /dev name can select another volume in a fresh test copy. Use the intended volume identity, then mount the saved work target.

The linked upstream-authored fstab manual is a newer displayed snapshot, not the unavailable pinned page. Only clean ext4/XFS metadata, exact inventory UUID strings and one mount per fixed directory/volume are modeled. Save stores raw text; Validate configuration and Test saved mounts are simulator actions, not Linux commands or a real reboot. The final state is graded; downtime and command history are not. Remount, stacking, nested mounts, LABEL/PARTUUID, escaped fields, inline comments and other options are unsupported. Only defaults/ro/rw/auto/noauto are modeled; defaults does not erase an explicit option. The supplied last two numbers are retained without performing their real operations. concepts.title: Attach a filesystem to a directory
concepts.text: A filesystem organizes stored data. Mounting attaches it at a directory called a mountpoint. Here the virtual volumes and directories are supplied, and every operation is simulated. There is no infrastructure to prepare.

concepts.title: Match the identity in the ticket
concepts.text: The ticket assigns each volume a purpose by UUID. blkid lists its current device name, UUID and filesystem type; it does not discover what a volume is used for. A /dev name may change. Copying the supplied lowercase UUID keeps the saved choice tied to that volume in this exercise.

concepts.title: Read one saved line
concepts.text: The file /etc/fstab holds saved mount instructions. Each line has six fields: source, mountpoint, type, options, dump frequency and check order. Match the type to the inventory. rw means writable, ro means read-only, and auto selects a fresh-session mount. defaults uses writable/automatic policy here. Keep the last two supplied numbers; this simulator performs no backup or filesystem check.

concepts.title: Save, mount, then verify
concepts.text: Type file changes in the editor and choose Save configuration. Validate configuration checks the saved file without mounting it. In the terminal, mount followed by a directory attaches its saved entry; mount alone lists current mounts. Test saved mounts tries independent copies with changed device names. It is not a real boot and cannot change your current session.

storage_teaching.example_description: Practice work is UUID aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaa1 at /practice-work, writable and automatic. Practice reports is UUID aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaa2 at /practice-reports, read-only and automatic. Repair only the missing work source and attach it; keep reports correct. Fill worked example fills this example editor only: save and run the mounting command yourself.

fixture.configuration:
UUID=aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaa9 /practice-work ext4 rw,auto 0 2
UUID=aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaa2 /practice-reports ext4 ro,auto 0 2

example_commands.explanation: List the supplied UUIDs and types beside their current simulated device names.
Read the saved file; it may differ from an unsaved editor draft.
After repairing and saving the work source, attach it at /practice-work.
List the live mounts and their current access policies.

storage_teaching.try_change: After the example passes, replace only its work source with /dev/practice1 and save. Validation still succeeds with current names, but Test saved mounts and Check example reveal the wrong volume after names change. Restore the practice work UUID and save to repair it.

scenarios.title: Make saved and live mount policies agree
scenarios.summary: Correct opposite work/archive policies in both the saved file and the current session.
scenarios.objective: Workspace is UUID 33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333 at /workspace and must be writable. Archive is UUID 44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444 at /archive and must be read-only. Both must remain automatic, correctly identified after device-name changes and mounted with the intended policies when finished. Repair the saved and live policies; keep identities, types and the supplied last two numbers unchanged.

steps: Inspect and repair the saved configuration
Make the live mounts match and verify
scenarios.explanation: The saved table controls later requests, while the live table describes the current attachments. Correcting only one table leaves part of the task unfinished. After each affected mount is recreated with the intended policy, the current session and independent fresh copies agree.

Fixing the saved policies does not alter the two existing mounts.
This subset applies a changed policy by unmounting the affected target and mounting it from the repaired saved file. Do this for both targets.

concepts.title: An access policy belongs to a mount
concepts.text: rw requests writable access and ro requests read-only access. This is separate from file ownership or permission bits: changing a saved mount policy is not a permission repair. The task checks both saved and current policies.

concepts.title: A saved edit does not change an existing mount
concepts.text: The saved file supplies future mount requests. A filesystem already mounted with ro stays ro after you save rw. Compare the editor, saved file and live table separately. An unsaved editor change has not even changed the saved instruction.

concepts.title: Apply the supported policy workflow
concepts.text: After saving and validating, unmount the affected directory, then mount it again to use the saved policy. This activity does not implement remount option merging; real Linux offers additional workflows. Either target order is valid, but both saved and current policies must be correct when finished.

storage_teaching.example_description: Practice build is UUID bbbbbbbb-bbbb-4bbb-8bbb-bbbbbbbbbbb1 at /practice-build and must be writable. Practice review is UUID bbbbbbbb-bbbb-4bbb-8bbb-bbbbbbbbbbb2 at /practice-review and must be read-only. Both are automatic and already mounted with the opposite policies. Fill only supplies corrected example text; save it and change each live mount yourself.

fixture.configuration:
UUID=bbbbbbbb-bbbb-4bbb-8bbb-bbbbbbbbbbb1 /practice-build ext4 ro 0 2
UUID=bbbbbbbb-bbbb-4bbb-8bbb-bbbbbbbbbbb2 /practice-review ext4 rw 0 2

example_commands.explanation: Inspect which policies have actually been saved.
Compare the live policies with the intended build/review policies.
Detach the existing build mount before requesting the new saved policy.
Attach build again using its saved entry; it should now be writable.
Detach the existing review mount; this does not delete the volume or saved entry.
Attach review with its saved read-only policy.

storage_teaching.try_change: After the example passes, save practice build as ro without changing its live mount. mount still shows it writable, but Check example fails the saved/fresh policy. Restore saved rw and retry. Notice that each view describes a different piece of state.

scenarios.title: Keep maintenance storage manual but available
scenarios.summary: Configure a manual-only maintenance mount without confusing automatic selection with current availability.
scenarios.objective:
Keep these final roles:
/work: UUID=55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555, ext4, writable and automatic.
/archive: UUID=66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666, ext4, read-only and automatic.
/maintenance: UUID=77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777, xfs, read-only and manual-only.
All three must be mounted now; fresh copies must mount only work and archive. Every saved entry, including maintenance, must retain its intended identity after device names change. Keep other policies, types and supplied last two numbers unchanged.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the first reported mismatch, then compare the ticket, saved file and live table. Saving, mounting and testing a fresh copy are different actions; retry after repairing the relevant state.
steps: Inspect and repair the saved configuration
Make the live mounts match and verify
scenarios.explanation: noauto controls automatic selection, not an explicit request. The current maintenance mount can be available read-only while independent copies skip it. Its saved UUID/type must still be correct, because a skipped row is not proof of a usable persistent configuration.
hints: Compare current availability with automatic selection. The ticket deliberately wants maintenance mounted here and absent in a fresh copy.
Use noauto on the maintenance entry; do not remove that entry or make the healthy work/archive entries manual.
Save the correct maintenance identity/type/policy, then explicitly mount /maintenance. Validate still checks manual rows.

concepts.title: Manual selection still permits an explicit mount
concepts.text: auto selects an entry in this activity's fresh-session plan. noauto skips that automatic selection, but you can still mount the directory explicitly. It does not mean the filesystem is unusable or that its saved entry can be deleted.

concepts.title: A skipped entry still needs a correct identity
concepts.text: A skipped row can contain a wrong UUID or type. Validate checks every saved row, including manual rows. The fresh checks also verify each saved identity with changed device names; an empty live mount at that target is not enough.

concepts.title: Keep the declared filesystem type
concepts.text: blkid reports TYPE as well as UUID. In this example the tool volume is xfs, while the other two are ext4; its saved type must match. These are clean metadata labels in this simulator, not filesystem creation, repair or an XFS implementation.

concepts.title: Current and fresh sessions can intentionally differ
concepts.text: Mount the manual tool volume for the current session, then test a fresh copy. The tool should remain mounted here but be skipped there. The fresh test uses a copy and never unmounts your current work.

storage_teaching.example_description: Keep practice work (UUID cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc1, ext4) writable at /practice-work and practice archive (UUID cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc2, ext4) read-only at /practice-archive, both automatic. Practice tool (UUID cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc3, xfs) must be mounted read-only now at /practice-tool but manual-only in fresh copies. Fill supplies only its corrected saved configuration.

fixture.configuration:
UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc1 /practice-work ext4 rw,auto 0 2
UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc2 /practice-archive ext4 ro,auto 0 2
UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc3 /practice-tool xfs ro,auto 0 2

example_solution:
storage {"kind":"Save","text":"UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc1 /practice-work ext4 rw,auto 0 2
UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc2 /practice-archive ext4 ro,auto 0 2
UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc3 /practice-tool xfs ro,noauto 0 2
"}

example_commands.explanation: Check the supplied UUID and TYPE for the manual tool volume.
Confirm the saved tool entry uses ro,noauto and the matching xfs type.
Explicitly attach the manual tool. noauto does not prevent this request.
Verify that all three practice targets are currently mounted with their intended policies.

storage_teaching.try_change: After passing, change only the practice tool type from xfs to ext4 and save. Validate and Check example must fail even though fresh copies skip that manual target. Restore xfs and save to repair it.

UUID=cccccccc-cccc-4ccc-8ccc-ccccccccccc3 /practice-tool ext4 ro,noauto 0 2

scenarios.title: Complete a stable storage handover
scenarios.summary: Combine identity, filesystem type, current policy and manual selection while retaining a healthy reports mount.
scenarios.objective:
Complete this handover; every saved role must survive changed device names:
/applications: UUID=88888888-8888-4888-8888-888888888888, ext4, writable, automatic and mounted now.
/archive: UUID=99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999, xfs, read-only, automatic and mounted now.
/maintenance: UUID=aaaaaaaa-aaaa-4aaa-8aaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa, ext4, read-only, manual-only and unmounted now.
/reports: UUID=bbbbbbbb-bbbb-4bbb-8bbb-bbbbbbbbbbbb, ext4, read-only, automatic and mounted now.
Repair every saved row and the live state. Leave all identities and supplied last two numbers unchanged. A skipped manual row still needs a correct persistent identity.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the first reported mismatch, then compare the ticket, saved file and live table. Saving, mounting and testing a fresh copy are different actions; retry after repairing the relevant state.
steps: Inspect and repair the saved configuration
Make the live mounts match and verify
scenarios.explanation: The handover succeeds only when every saved entry identifies the intended volume with its declared type and policy, and the current live table matches the ticket. The archive requires a new live read-only mount; the healthy roles do not need a change. Maintenance stays configured but unmounted. Independent name changes test saved identity for all rows, including manual ones; this is not a system boot or a data-integrity test.
hints: Compare each ticket row with blkid, the saved file and mount output. Current connection names alone do not establish stable identity.
The archive has both saved-file and current-mount problems; changing the type or policy in one place is not enough.
The maintenance row is skipped automatically, but its UUID still needs repair. Keep it unmounted here; preserve the final reports identity and read-only policy.

concepts.title: Check the complete ticket
concepts.text: A handover combines identity, type, access policy, current availability and automatic selection. A mount can succeed with the wrong volume, and a valid saved file can coexist with a stale live policy. Inspect each final role rather than trusting one success message.

concepts.title: Do not overlook a manual entry
concepts.text: noauto entries still need a correct source/type. Their saved identities are checked in every changed-name copy even when mounting is skipped. In this task maintenance is correctly configured but must remain unmounted in the actual session too.

concepts.title: Repair and verify without inventing new operations
concepts.text: Use the same editor, validation, mount listing and unmount/mount workflow as before. Fresh-session tests are independent simulated copies, not a real reboot. The task checks final state; it does not measure downtime or perform application/data verification.

storage_teaching.example_description: For this smaller handover, /practice-service is UUID dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd1, ext4, writable/automatic/mounted. /practice-archive is UUID dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd2, xfs, read-only/automatic/mounted. /practice-maintenance is UUID dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd3, ext4, read-only/manual-only/unmounted. Correct every saved identity/type/policy and the stale live archive policy. Fill supplies only the corrected example file.

fixture.configuration:
/dev/practice1 /practice-service ext4 rw,auto 0 2
UUID=dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd2 /practice-archive ext4 rw 0 2
UUID=dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd9 /practice-maintenance ext4 ro,noauto 0 2

example_solution:
storage {"kind":"Save","text":"UUID=dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd1 /practice-service ext4 rw,auto 0 2
UUID=dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd2 /practice-archive xfs ro,auto 0 2
UUID=dddddddd-dddd-4ddd-8ddd-ddddddddddd3 /practice-maintenance ext4 ro,noauto 0 2
"}

example_commands.explanation: Inspect the supplied identities and declared types before repairing the handover file.
Read the saved plan, including the manual maintenance row.
Compare current live mounts with the complete ticket.
Remove the stale writable archive mount; leave the other final roles correct.
Use the repaired saved archive entry to attach it read-only.

storage_teaching.try_change: After passing, explicitly mount /practice-maintenance. Its saved manual policy and fresh-copy absence are still correct, but the current-session handover requirement now fails. Unmount /practice-maintenance to retry.
